name: Pogs Game
description: A heavy slammer, a stack of original illustrated discs, and a small collection worth keeping. Flick, flip and collect across four tabletop game modes.

assets.credit: Original Odd Company artwork, slammers and tabletop rendering

compatibility: Canvas 2D, Pointer Events, ResizeObserver and requestAnimationFrame. No third-party runtime, remote artwork, fonts or audio.

Mouse, pen and captured touch. Drag from the slammer toward the stack, or tap to aim and press Strike. Keyboard arrows aim, Shift makes smaller adjustments, Space strikes; ordinary buttons bank winnings.
A single visible canvas projects rotating front/back textures and physical edges. Original artwork and the table are cached; at most 16 discs animate together.
Hidden tabs, offscreen previews, the shared pause control and album/builder views suspend animation and CPU turns without catch-up. An idle table has no animation loop.

Reduced motion resolves the flight directly to its genuine result. Collecting, aiming, CPU turns and all settings remain usable. The collection stays local, with JSON export/import and a clear/undo control.
notes: Odd Company is an original tabletop toy. Twelve editions feature a moon moth, sun-eating fish, orbital planet, midnight flower, watchful cloud, solar face, tiny ship, lizard, shell, paper tiger, firefly and observatory. No branded disc art or slammer designs are used.

Discs begin face down. A gesture sets impact position and power from travel distance and velocity. Tap-to-aim and button or keyboard strikes use the inspector power setting. Missing the stack produces no flips.

The controlled impact model combines overlap, slammer mass, tilt, edge leverage, friction, table surface, stack depth and stable disc variation. It computes a deterministic flight and final half-turn count. The rendered landing orientation determines scoring; there is no separate random reward roll.

Bank face-up discs, then watch the remaining discs restack. CPU mode alternates turns; Mica uses the same slammer and impact function, and only the human player’s winnings enter their collection. Practice and collection rounds have no stakes or paid rewards.

The album shows front and reverse artwork, collected counts, edition tiers, and missing designs. Collection play deals missing editions first. The builder supports duplicates and a meaningful bottom-to-top order, with up to sixteen discs.

Five presets, full table/ordered-stack JSON, album JSON and source export are included. Shared presets save inspector settings; local table export also saves chosen disc IDs. Album data is independent of settings and rounds.
reuse: DiscGame and planStrike in model.js are browser-independent. Supply your own catalog, ordered stack, normalized settings and impact point. Semantic events report strikes, landings, collection and completion.

createDiscTable(canvas, settings, hooks) adds projection, cached textures, pointer and keyboard input, visibility-controlled animation and cleanup. A drawDisc callback supplies custom front and reverse artwork.

The source export includes the original art, reusable model and renderer, optional HTML UI, five presets, documented schemas and a neutral three-color custom-disc example. There are no Tampa-specific runtime imports.
